title: Normalized affine stalk model in a single fine chart
statement: Let $X$ have a sheaf of commutative monoids with sharp stalks, let $c:X|_V\simeq S(A)$ be one fine chart, and let $z\in V$. Let $U$ be a smallest open neighborhood of $z$ in $X$, and suppose its actual stalk $P=\mathcal P_{X,z}$ is fine, with conventions [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] and canonical-section pullback [lem-trf-affine-fan-hom-universal]. There exists an isomorphism $\iota:X|_U\simeq S(P)$ local in both directions such that for each $p\in P$ the germ of the pullback of its canonical section is $p$. There is a morphism $k:S(P)\to S(A)$ induced, on primes and numerator germs, by the actual chart-section germ homomorphism $A\to P$, and $k$ followed by the inverse chart and open inclusion equals $\iota^{-1}$ followed by the inclusion of $U$, as full sheafed-space morphisms. No uniqueness or comparison of different charts is asserted.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood], in the selected chart U is D(s), and Q=A[s inverse] is A localized at the prime complement. By [lem-trf-fine-fan-chart-stalk-coordinates], identify B=Q modulo units with the actual stalk P by the specified numerator germs. The supplied fineness of P makes this a fine sharp affine model.

proof.text: Extend a prime of A avoiding s to fractions whose numerators are in that prime; contract in the opposite direction. Equal fraction expressions have equal numerator membership because s avoids the prime. Denominators are units, so extension and contraction are inverse. Ideals of Q are stable under multiplication by units in both directions, so image and inverse image under Q to B also biject prime ideals. Both bijections preserve basic opens. This gives the homeomorphism D(s) to Spec B.

proof.text: For t in Q and b its class in B, compare B[b inverse] modulo units and Q[t inverse] modulo units. The forward map sends numerator classes to numerator classes; the reverse map factors Q to Q[t inverse] modulo units through B, since units vanish, and then through the localization and its sharpening. Both composites fix numerators and kill denominator units, hence are identities. The same formulas commute with further localization.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections] on corresponding basic opens and the maps of Step 3 to get inverse compatible section maps. Extend them by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis], then transport through the chart and the actual-stalk equivalence. The stalk maps are isomorphisms and hence local. Numerator preservation gives the displayed normalization. Contraction of primes and the same numerator formulas give IsAffineMap for the map to the original A chart. Its section maps are exactly the restriction maps, proving the full sheafed-space square.

theorem fineFan_chart_minimal_affine (X : SheafedSpace CommMonCat.{u})
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsSharp (stalk X.presheaf x))
    (c : Chart X) (z : X) (hc : z ∈ c.openSet)
    (U : Opens X) (hz : z ∈ U)
    (hU : ∀ V : Opens X, z ∈ V → U ≤ V)
    (hP : IsFine (stalk X.presheaf z)) :
    ∃ ι : X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding ≅ affine (stalk X.presheaf z),
      IsLocalMorphism ι.hom ∧ IsLocalMorphism ι.inv ∧
      (∀ p : stalk X.presheaf z,
        germ X.presheaf U z hz
          ((X.presheaf.map (eqToHom (Opens.isOpenEmbedding_obj_top U).symm).op)
            (affinePullback ι.hom p)) = p) ∧
      ∃ k : affine (stalk X.presheaf z) ⟶ affine c.monoid,
        IsAffineMap
          ((germ X.presheaf c.openSet z hc).hom.comp
            ((X.presheaf.map
              (eqToHom (Opens.isOpenEmbedding_obj_top c.openSet).symm).op).hom.comp
                (affinePullback c.iso.hom))) k ∧
        k ≫ c.iso.inv ≫ X.ofRestrict c.openSet.isOpenEmbedding =
          ι.inv ≫ X.ofRestrict U.isOpenEmbedding
